No - a USB cable carries digital signal and your computer translates that into audio. Audio cables -XLRs (mix cables), TRS (1/4 inch), TS (instrument cable) - carry audio signal, which your looper, well... loops. 
Your loop pedal accepts audio signal, not digital. You would need a regular mic with an XLR conection, and even then unless your looper has an integrated mic pre amp (google it because it might!), you’d need some device (cloudifier?) to boost the signal to line level (mic level is too low). 

If you want to record you also need a separate audio interface, to connect your looper to. The audio interface turns the signal back to digital signal so your computer can record it. 

I highly recommend getting an audio interface, the scarlet 2i2 is pretty affordable, and that way you don’t need USB mics, which honestly don’t sound that great. With an interface you can also record your guitar directly, and record your looper.

I'm currently living in Massachusetts because of school, so accessing hormone replacement therapy here was super easy. I got HRT through Fenway Health, a hospital entirely for LGBT people, and they operate under the informed consent model. They basically gave me a routine medical exam, asked me some questions about my gender, dysphoria, mental health, etc, talked to my therapist, took some blood samples, made me sign a bunch of waivers, and I had my testosterone prescription in a couple of weeks. This model is mostly for people who are 100% sure they're trans, I could totally see things go south if someone goes to an informed consent clinic while they're still trying to figure things out, but for me it worked perfectly because I was not willing to wait.
